text:
alice.pm: Ok team — quick rebaseline convo. Customer escalations + infra perf regression mean the original v1 date is optimistic. I think we should: freeze a razor-thin MVP for launch and defer noncritical v1 pillars to a v1.1. Proposing a 3-week shift and a strict cutlist. Thoughts?

ben.eng: agree on a freeze, +1 on 3-week slip. Reality: the KV cache fix is the blocker for sustained QPS. If we don't ship it, we need throttles which hurts UX.

carol.design: If we cut anything from v1, we must keep the onboarding flow and token-cost transparency. Those are user-visible. Everything else can be tagged for v1.1.

david.pmm: Echo onboarding and transparency. Also call out integrations that anchor early adopters — we should keep at least 1 SSO variant for pilot customers.

alice.pm: Good call. Proposal (short):
```
MUST (ship in MVP): onboarding flow, token-cost telemetry, basic SSO (SAML only), model pinning, error fallback policies
SHOULD (v1.0 target if capacity allows): advanced routing, batch-caching advisory, RBAC refinements
DEFER (v1.1): quantization profiles UI, extended observability retention, additional SSO variants
```
This is intentionally strict.

ben.eng: That MUST list is implementable in ~3 weeks if we stop adding new product work. Risk: canary rollout might take extra days. I'll coordinate with infra to parallelize KV fix + telemetry.

emma.pm: Can we map each MUST to a single owner and a minimal acceptance criteria? I can run a brief RAID log and weekly checkpoints.

alice.pm: Yes. I'll assign owners after this thread. For acceptance: a short smoke script + perf gate: p95 latency under 300ms for typical pilot load, token cost within 15% of forecast.

carol.design: UX ask: minimize UI churn for onboarding — toggles not full redesign. I'll ship microcopy and the onboarding checklist this week.

david.pmm: Also customer comms: I'll draft an email explaining staged launch (MVP -> v1.1) emphasizing stability and roadmap. Want to share by EOD Friday.

ben.eng: FYI release-bot shows next window has a hardware maintenance on week 2 of the slip window. We should avoid scheduling heavy canaries then. :warning:

release-bot: scheduled-maintenance: region-us-west-2 GPUs maintenance window 2026-04-14 02:00-06:00 UTC (may affect canary throughput).

alice.pm: Noted. Let's target canaries before that or after. Final ask: if anyone objects to the strict cutlist, speak up now; otherwise I'll publish a single-slice plan and owners by noon tomorrow. :thumbsup:

ben.eng: no objection.

carol.design: no objection.

emma.pm: no objection.

david.pmm: no objection.

alice.pm: Great — publishing plan and owners in #product-updates in the morning.
